leads.title: Federal law on 'propaganda of non-traditional sexual relationships' (2013, expanded 2022)
leads.documents: National legal status criminalizing distribution of materials promoting non-traditional relationships and gender transition; applies in Udmurtia as federal law
leads.detail: Cited as passed 2013 criminalising distribution among minors; expanded 2022 to apply to anyone regardless of age and to prohibit materials that make minors interested in gender transitions

leads.title: July 2023 Russian law banning gender transition
leads.documents: National ban on transgender healthcare and legal gender recognition relevant to trans-visitor safety in Udmurtia
leads.detail: Cited as enacted July 2023; prohibited both gender-affirming surgery and legal gender recognition outright; preceded by April-May 2023 Duma proposals cited to Minister of Justice Konstantin Chuychenko and Nina Ostanina

leads.title: 2024 law banning adoption of Russian children by citizens/permanent residents of countries that allow gender transitions
leads.documents: Federal enforcement machinery around gender-transition policy
leads.detail: Cited as passed in 2024 banning adoption by citizens or permanent residents of countries that allow gender transitions

leads.title: Supreme Court of Russia ruling November 2023 designating 'the international LGBT public movement' as extremist
leads.documents: Criminalization of LGBT activism, participation, funding, and display of symbols like rainbow flag; federal enforcement applicable in Udmurtia
leads.detail: Cited as November 2023 ruling following Ministry of Justice lawsuit; formally added 22 March 2024 to 'unified list of terrorist and extremist organizations and persons' as 'international LGBT social movement and its structural units'

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - Fedotova and Others v. Russia (2021)
leads.documents: Court ruling that failure to offer any legal recognition to same-sex relationships violates human rights
leads.detail: Cited as 2021 case Fedotova and Others v. Russia in Strasbourg; notes Russia left the court in 2022

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - 2010 ruling on pride parade bans (Alexeyev)
leads.documents: Finding of discrimination by Russian cities refusing to authorize pride parades, showing enforcement pattern
leads.detail: Cited as 2010 fine against Russia after systemic refusal of permits; brought by Nikolay Alexeyev over Moscow Pride; Moscow City Court August 2012 upheld yearly ban through 2012 contravening ruling

leads.title: United Nations Human Rights Council expert panel report - 13 April 2017
leads.documents: UN condemnation of wave of torture and killings of gay men in Chechnya as example of federal enforcement failure
leads.detail: Cited as report issued 13 April 2017 by panel of five expert advisors to the UN Human Rights Council

leads.title: Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) report - December 2018
leads.documents: Institutional confirmation that persecution of LGBTQ persons took place and was ignored by authorities
leads.detail: Cited as report released December 2018 confirming claims of persecution

leads.title: Novaya Gazeta report - 1 April 2017 on Chechnya anti-gay purges
leads.documents: Documented incident of forced disappearances, secret abductions, imprisonment, torture and extrajudicial killings
leads.detail: Cited as 1 April 2017 reporting that since February 2017 over 100 men detained and tortured and at least three died; called 'prophylactic sweep' citing Chechen special services sources

leads.title: ILGA-Europe rankings - 2016, 2019, 2024
leads.documents: Institutional human-rights assessment of LGBTQ legal climate in Russia applicable to Udmurtia
leads.detail: Cited as 2016 rated second least LGBTQ-friendly in Europe; May 2019 placed 46th of 49; 2024 ranked worst of 49 surveyed, followed by Turkey and Azerbaijan
